title: The Servant Who Had No Mercy
bigIdea: God forgives us so much — He wants us to forgive others too.

memoryVerse.text: Forgive each other, just as God forgave you.

moral.lesson: The king forgave the servant a huge debt he could never repay — but then that same servant refused to forgive his friend a tiny one. Jesus told this story to show us something important: God forgives us for so many things, so He wants us to forgive other people too, even when it's hard.
moral.application: When someone hurts you or says they're sorry, you can choose to forgive them — just like God forgives you, again and again. Forgiving sets your heart free.

style: Flat-color children's cartoon storybook illustration, simple rounded shapes, soft warm colors, thick clean black outlines, bright and friendly, gentle lighting, 16:9 landscape composition, no text or words in the image, no letters.
character: the king: a kind man with a crown and a royal red and gold robe; and a servant in a plain brown tunic. Keep the king and the servant looking the same in every picture.

beats.scene: Peter, a friendly fisherman with a beard, is talking with Jesus who has brown hair and a beard in a cream robe. Peter looks curious and is asking a question. Calm, sunny outdoor scene.
text: One day Jesus' friend Peter had a question. “Jesus,” he asked, “how many times should I forgive someone who is unkind to me? Seven times?”
Peter thought seven times sounded like a lot! But Jesus said, “Not seven times — many, many more than that!”
Then Jesus told a story to help Peter understand.

beats.scene: A king on a throne kindly forgiving a servant who is kneeling and bowing low with his hands together, begging. A huge pile of gold sits nearby. The king reaches out with a gentle, forgiving gesture. Grand throne room.
text: There was a servant who owed the king a HUGE amount of money — more than he could ever, ever pay back.
The servant fell down on his knees and begged, “Please, be patient with me!”
The king felt sorry for him. “I forgive your whole debt,” the king said kindly. Just like that, the servant didn't owe a single coin. He was free!

beats.scene: The same servant outside grabbing another man (his friend) roughly by the collar, looking angry, while the friend looks frightened. A small coin pouch is nearby. Tense street scene.
text: But on his way out, that same servant met a friend who owed him just a tiny bit of money.
Instead of being kind, the servant grabbed his friend and shouted, “Pay me back right now!”
His friend dropped to his knees. “Please, be patient with me!” he begged — the very same words the servant had used with the king. But the servant would not listen.

beats.scene: The angry servant pointing toward a small jail while two guards lead away the frightened friend. The servant has his arms crossed and looks hard-hearted. Gloomy scene.
text: The servant refused to forgive his friend even a little bit.
He had his friend thrown into jail until every last coin could be paid back.
How sad! The servant had just been forgiven so much, but he would not share even a little of that kindness.

beats.scene: The king back on his throne looking serious and disappointed, speaking firmly to the servant who now looks ashamed and sorry, head down. Grand throne room, serious mood.
text: When the king heard what had happened, he called the servant back.
“I forgave you everything when you begged me,” the king said. “Shouldn't you have forgiven your friend the same way?”
God forgives us for so much. He wants us to forgive other people too.
